newsitem.title: PERU: Police warn Japanese media in Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Police warn Japanese media in Peru crisis.

text.p: Peruvian police warned members of the Japanese media Tuesday not to attempt to enter the captured official residence in Lima again.
Police chief Col. Fernando Zapata told Japanese Fuji TV to tell other media from Japan to stay away from the diplomatic compound where Marxist rebels hold 74 VIP hostages.
"Talk about this among yourselves. Tell others of the Japanese press to not enter," he said.

Zapata also said two Asian-looking journalists were reported to have been hanging around a nearby house early Tuesday from where two members of Japan's TV Asahi managed to sneak past police and into the residence Jan 7.

Members of the Japanese media stirred up the Lima hostage crisis twice earlier this month by entering the besieged official residence stormed by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels Dec. 17.
Their actions irked both Peruvian and Japanese governments but won the admiration of many fellow journalists.
